results.summary_before: This project implements a 4-bit binary multiplier using a combinational array structure. It multiplies two 4-bit numbers by generating partial products and summing them with full adders. The design is purely digital and produces an 8-bit product. It is a structural implementation suitable for learning about binary multiplication.

results.summary_before: This analog block implements a very slow ring oscillator whose output is brought out on two analog pins. It is used by powering the board at 1.8 V and observing the signal on analog pins 0 and 1. The documentation is extremely thin, giving only a one-line description and no schematic, frequency measurement, or test results, so the exact topology and performance are unclear. The design is notable for its extremely low oscillation frequency and its use of the analog I/O pins.

results.summary_before: This is a systolic array accelerator that drives a VGA display to show visual patterns. It includes a graphics output and uses a PRNG for pattern generation. The design is implemented in Verilog and targets the Tiny Tapeout platform. It is intended for demoscene-style visual showcases.
results.summary: This project implements Wolfram Rule 30, a 1D cellular automaton, in hardware. It updates a 320-bit generation register each row and displays 480 generations on a VGA monitor using the Tiny VGA pinout. Two input pins select among four colour palettes. It produces the characteristic asymmetric triangular chaos pattern expanding from a centre seed.

results.summary_before: This design is a clock generator and display driver. It uses a 7-segment display and includes timer and button inputs. The design also includes a real-time clock (RTC) functionality.
results.summary: This design is a multiplexed digital clock that counts hours in 24-hour format and minutes, with dots indicating 15/30/45/60 seconds. It drives a 4-digit 7-segment display via multiplexing, using uo_out for segments and uio_out[3:0] for digit selection. Two pull-up button inputs increase hours or minutes, and inputs configure anode/cathode and output negation. It has been partially tested on silicon.

results.summary_before: This project is a memory design with SRAM, 7-segment display, decoder, and multiplexer, created with Wokwi. It has three address bits, eight bidirectional data pins, and a read/write control, with outputs also driving a 7-segment display. To test, users connect address and data pins, set R/W high and clock to write, or set R/W low to read without clocking. The design is intended for educational purposes.
results.summary: This project uses D flip-flops with reset to sequence the outer six segments of a 7-segment display in a spin pattern. A multiplexer, controlled by input IN0, allows the sequence to stop after six shifts, and further multiplexers reverse the direction and clear the display on reset. It targets a 2 Hz clock and is intended to run on the Wokwi simulator. Test it by setting the clock and observing the display while pressing reset or toggling IN0.
